memory_candidates.content: When two or more concurrent tasks must edit the SAME shared bash function signature or the SAME large prose SKILL.md file, partition by POSITIONAL SLOT (for a function) or by STAGE/REGION plus append-only list bullets (for a SKILL.md), never by file. Concrete instance: skill_postflight_update's signature (1 task_number, 2 operation, 3 session_id, 4 status, 5 phase_check_mode) let one sibling task own positional 6 while this task added ONLY `local status_clamp_mode="${7:-}"`, reading position 7 directly and never touching 6 -- a positional gap is harmless in bash regardless of landing order. For skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md, this task added a brand-new stage heading (Stage 2b) plus append-only bullets to Stage 1/Stage MT-1's existing lists, and referenced sibling-owned Stage 4 handler bodies BY HEADING POINTER rather than editing them -- a scoped `git diff` after the edit (checking hunks land ONLY in the new/appended regions) is the verification that proves no collision occurred.

A SKILL.md file in this codebase is prose-plus-bash DOCUMENTATION an agent follows procedurally turn-by-turn (each fenced bash block is something the agent executes via its own Bash tool across many separate tool calls) -- it is never literally concatenated and run as one script. But when authoring a multi-branch decision (an if/elif/else) inside such a file, write it as ONE single flowing fenced bash block, not three separately-fenced fragments with prose interleaved between an `if ... then` fragment and its `elif`/`else`/`fi` continuation. A split-fence if/elif/else leaves each individual fence syntactically incomplete, which breaks any later `bash -n` extraction test over that exact block (this repo has precedent for exactly this kind of extraction, e.g. test-loop-guard-budget-override.sh) even though the file itself is never executed as a whole. Prose bullets ABOVE the single fenced block can still narrate each branch's semantics at length; only the code itself needs to stay unified.

To test a source-store-only edit in a repo where .claude/ is a gitignored deploy artifact regenerated from agent-system/extensions/**, build a scratchpad/fixture harness whose .claude/scripts/ tree is populated from the DEPLOYED tree for every non-edited dependency, then OVERLAID (overwritten) with the source-store copies of exactly the files under test, before pointing SKILL_REPO_ROOT and cwd at the fixture root. This is necessary because dependency chains are often multi-hop: sourcing a source-store entry point directly is not enough if that file's OWN internal `source lib/foo.sh` call still resolves deploy-first relative to SKILL_REPO_ROOT/cwd -- a partial fix (source-store entry point, deploy-first internals) produces a 'command not found' on a newly-added function rather than a clean pass/fail signal, which is the exact failure signature of a stale internal-dependency load. When authoring a NEW regression-suite file for such an edit, invert the deploy-first/source-store-fallback candidate order ONLY for the specific files under test (source-store first, deploy fallback) while keeping deploy-tree provenance for every unrelated fixture dependency -- and make the resolved absolute path of each inverted candidate an explicit, echoed assertion (never merely implicit) as the FIRST case in the suite, exiting 2 (environment error) rather than 1 (test failure) on a miss, since a wrong-copy load means the whole suite would silently validate the wrong code.
